property_summary: NETM may only successfully complete when invoked by the contract owner (the deployer, i.e. the test contract); the flipped mutant lets any non-owner succeed, so the rule 'success implies caller == owner' fails for a fuzzed non-owner caller.

After the owner initializes the token sale via NETM(), the owner's balance must equal c.totalDistributed(); the mutant instead assigns totalRemaining, which diverges from totalDistributed once any airdrop has occurred.

After ownership is transferred to any address actor and that actor calls NETM(), the contract must credit the (new) owner with exactly totalDistributed tokens; the mutant deletes that assignment so the owner's balance stays 0.

A token distribution adds _amount to the recipient's existing balance (balance_after == balance_before + amount), so after the owner initializes balances via NETM and then claims tokens via getTokens, c.balanceOf(owner) equals totalDistributed plus the granted value; the mutant overwrites the balance with only the granted amount, breaking this for the owner.
